meta.outlierRule: Outlier = 10K+ views and 5× the creator's median views over their last 30 posts (measured for the strongest candidates only).

insights.title: Movie scene + one line about the payoff
insights.body: “How life feels when you quit Zyn and your natural dopamine comes back” over a famous film clip. One 182-follower account has 4 outliers with this (up to 732× its median); the same format worked with AI Sonic and Wolf of Wall Street. It's cheap and repeatable — the line names a concrete payoff: dopamine, control, sleep.

insights.title: Admit the downside
insights.body: “I quit nicotine after 10+ years and notice nothing but weight gain” (1,037× median) and “I quit zyns 6 weeks ago and life hasn't improved at all” (97×). Honest disappointment beats the generic success story — and opens a perfect reply for a quitting app.

insights.title: Credibility + an unusual method in sentence one
insights.body: “As somebody that vaped for six years and quit two years ago, here's what actually works” (564×) and the hot-sauce-as-punishment method (724×, 1.3M). Time served + the promise of something specific and unexpected.

insights.title: Day-N diary
insights.body: “Day 7 of no nicotine… last night was a battle” (91×), a silent day-counter face video (288×, 1.5M) and “Day 1 without drugs” (62×). Raw check-ins, especially craving moments, turn one post into a series people come back for.

insights.title: Show the damage — gums, heart, lungs
insights.body: A dentist pointing at a pouch on gums (365×, 1.1M), a 3D anatomy “what one pouch does” (384K), “My gums before I started zynning” (70×). A close-up of the mouth stops the scroll.

insights.title: Competitor app accounts: listicle slideshows
insights.body: QuitPouch, Clean Streak, Oneless, Pouchless and others run faceless accounts with under 100 followers that reach 10–80K with slide 1 lines like “5 ZYN side effects people ignore” or “The real cost of a year on zyns”. Reach is real but engagement is ~0.5% — views without a community.

items.author: emilyyminnickk
items.caption: Quit the vape cold turkey 2 years ago here’s what I did 🫶🏼 IF I CAN YOU CAN!!!! #vape #quitvaping #fyp #quitnic #sobertiktok
items.hook: “As somebody that vaped for literally six years and quit as of two years ago yesterday, here's what actually works.”
items.transcript: As somebody that vaped for literally six years and quit as of two years ago yesterday, here's what actually works. One, patches, no go. Nicotine gum, no go. My biggest advice is to download the audiobook, Alan Carr's Easy Way to Quit Vaping. Takes about four to six hours to listen to. You don't have to quit before you listen to the book. It actually advocates for you not to. I did, but looking back, I wish I wouldn't have. I wish I would have just listened to the book with peace of mind without going through all the withdrawals. Okay, so download the book, the premise, and I'll give you kind of a high level. I was a psychology major, so I believe your mind is very, very powerful. And the book itself goes through every single social fad, what we believe culturally, the vape is doing for us. It's an appetite suppressant. I'm irritable without the vape, etc, etc. You will unravel all of those thoughts while listening to the book. So I'll put it here. Download that. Or if you're a physical book reader. I'm not. Order the physical book. Either way, you gotta listen to it. Secondly, like I said, the patches. I hate to break it to you. Nicotine is a drug that's quickest in, quickest out. So what that means is the hit that you take immediately obviously causes that head rush and all the things. Right? The reason that in the morning after Like, going to bed for a good eight hours rest. That vape hits the hardest is because your body is already going through withdrawals at that point. Okay, there is a statistic, I believe it's like 70% out of your system by the time eight hours passes. 72 hours passes, it's completely out of your system. It's only mental from there forward back. Check me on that. But I know that they explain it in the book as well. If you can get past the first 72 hours, knowing that that is on the other side. And everything after that point is not a physical withdrawal, it's a mental withdrawal. That was the switch for me. I was like, okay, 72 hours of hell, I'm expecting it. I got it. After that, I'm in the clear. And I will say for three weeks, yeah, it's difficult. But after those first 72 hours, the difficulty becomes the association. So two things. One, the association of, like, hand mouth movement. Every time you pick up the vape, bring it to your mouth, take a hit, that movement associates with your brain. So replacing that with something, for me, what I did was replaced it with my water bottle of choice. Right? Like every single time I thought about hitting the vape, bring the water bottle up, take a big chug. Bonus points if it's ice cold and kind of tickles the back of your throat as the vape did. And if you Want to put like, flavorings in your water? Do it. Secondly, the oral fixation, cause obviously can't just like, sit there and chug water all day. Mints, gum, anything that can keep your mouth occupied was helpful to me. Wintergreen Mints. Great. Any minty gum, because I was doing mint flavored vapes. That was helpful. And then lastly, I think, guys, it's just time. If you are able to tell someone, tell your friends, tell your family. Throw out all of the vapes in your house, the car one, the emergency one, all of the batteries, toss it out. Toss it out. And know that after 72 hours, you were over the hump. After three weeks, you're no longer a vapor. You no longer have to worry about social gatherings. Is it acceptable for me to vape in this place? Hit the bathroom because I need to sneak this vape in. Or I was worried about, like, going on a boat on the lake? what if my vape falls in the water and I'm stranded for four hours? Like, all of those anxiety is that come with it, gone. Think about your life after the fact when you're not chained to that little device. You got this. I promise.

items.caption: Pro tips for quiting nicotine pouches like zyns is gradually taper down the amount you take. I used to do 10 ish a day and went cold turkey but relapsed about 5 times… i realized my brain wasn’t ready for that switch, so I instead gradually reduced the amount I was taking, so I would take my last pouch in 3 weeks. items.author: skelyfact
items.caption: What happens to your lungs if you use nicotine pouches (Zyn) every single day? #zyn #nicotine #lungs #humanbody #foryoupage
items.hook: “When you tuck just one nicotine pouch under your lip, it's not just your mouth that reacts.”
items.transcript: When you tuck just one nicotine pouch under your lip, it's not just your mouth that reacts. This concentrated nicotine first enters your bloodstream through the gums, then travels straight to your heart, causing your pulse to spike instantly. From the heart, the nicotine is pumped into your lungs, reaching the delicate, branching pathways. Even without smoke, these chemical particles begin triggering inflammation inside the airways. Inside the lungs, there are tiny hair like structures called cilia that help keep your system clean. But daily nicotine can weaken these cilia, disturbing the lungs natural cleaning system. Over time, this systemic irritation continues to build up inside the airways. As cardiovascular strain increases, you may feel heavy breathing, chest tightness, or racing heart. The small air sacs in the lungs are vital for oxygen exchange, but constant nicotine flow can affect them too. When you use these every day, your body struggles to push this chemical stress back out. Nicotine pouches are not harmless. Choose your health, protect your heart and lungs, and try to stay away from daily use. Because every breath counts. Don't let your health go up in a glow. Follow scaly fact. Account for more.
